MCQ
Which covalent bond is made when alanine is attached to its tRNA?
Ester between the amino acid carboxyl and terminal ribose OH|Peptide bond to the anticodon|Phosphodiester bond to A76 base|Hydrogen bond to C75
The amino acid carboxyl forms an ester with a ribose hydroxyl. Peptide bonds connect amino acids; phosphodiesters connect nucleotides; hydrogen bonding is noncovalent.
MCQ
The notation Val-tRNA^Ile describes which molecule?
Isoleucine attached to valine tRNA|Valine attached to isoleucine tRNA|Uncharged isoleucine tRNA|A valine codon in mRNA
The prefix identifies actual cargo; the superscript identifies the normal adaptor identity. Valine on an isoleucine adaptor is a mischarged species in the ordinary system.
MCQ
Where is the amino acid attachment site of a canonical mature tRNA?
Anticodon position 34|D loop|Terminal adenosine A76|Discriminator base 73
A76 ribose provides the 2′ and 3′ hydroxyls; position 73 contributes to recognition but is not the conventional attachment site.
MCQ
Which sequence is antiparallel and complementary to 5′-GCU-3′?
G pairs C, C pairs G and U pairs A; the strands run antiparallel. Written 5′ to 3′ the anticodon is AGC, not CGA.
MCQ
Which tRNA region contains the G3·U70 determinant in bacterial tRNA^Ala?
Acceptor stem|Anticodon loop|Variable loop|D loop
Positions 3 and 70 pair near the acceptor end, spatially separated from the anticodon. Their identity can be critical even when the anticodon is unchanged.
MCQ
What distinguishes isoacceptor tRNAs?
They always have identical anticodons|They carry the same amino acid but can read different synonymous codons|They always carry two amino acids|They are different ribosomal subunits
Isoacceptors share amino acid identity but can differ in anticodon and sequence. Isodecoders have the same anticodon but distinct body sequences.
MCQ
Which intermediate is formed during ordinary amino acid activation?
Aminoacyl-ADP|Aminoacyl-GTP|Aminoacyl-AMP|Peptidyl-rRNA
The carboxylate reacts at the alpha phosphate of ATP, leaving PPi and forming the adenylate. Neither ADP nor GTP is the standard intermediate.
MCQ
What does hydrolysis of PPi accomplish?
Reads an anticodon|Cleaves the tRNA backbone|Adds CCA|Helps drive the activation reaction forward
Removal of a product favors forward activation. Pyrophosphatase does not decode RNA or catalyze CCA addition.
MCQ
What is the usual initial transfer site of class I synthetases?
2′-OH of A76|5′ phosphate of position 1|Anticodon base 35|3′-OH of C75
Class I enzymes usually transfer to the terminal 2′ hydroxyl. The 3′ hydroxyl of A76 is typical of class II, with exceptions.
MCQ
Which statement about class II PheRS is correct?
It uses no ATP|It is a notable exception that initially acylates 2′-OH|It is a ribosomal protein|It catalyzes CCA addition
PheRS is structurally class II yet initially uses the 2′ hydroxyl. Classification depends on protein fold, not an exceptionless transfer-site rule.
MCQ
Which substrate is hydrolyzed in pre-transfer editing?
Free correct tRNA|mRNA|Incorrect aminoacyl adenylate|Peptide bond
Pre-transfer editing acts before RNA esterification. Post-transfer editing hydrolyzes an aminoacyl-tRNA ester; neither process edits the message.
MCQ
Post-transfer editing ordinarily produces which pair?
AMP and a peptide|ADP and PPi|Two RNA fragments|Free amino acid and deacylated tRNA
Hydrolysis breaks the aminoacyl ester, leaving the nucleotide backbone intact and restoring a usable acceptor hydroxyl.
MCQ
Which is the canonical double-sieve example?
IleRS removes Val from tRNA^Ile|RNA polymerase removes valine|Ribosomal RNA charges Ile|ValRS converts Ile to Val
IleRS can reject valine through editing after imperfect initial discrimination. The other choices confuse charging, decoding or amino acid conversion.
MCQ
Why does an editing site need selectivity for incorrect cargo?
To increase transcription|To avoid wasting correctly charged product|To create a new anticodon|To consume all cellular ATP
Correct charging must survive; nonspecific hydrolysis of cognate products would reduce supply and waste energy.
MCQ
Which statement about tRNA recognition is accurate?

All synthetases recognize only the anticodon|The CCA sequence uniquely identifies each amino acid|Identity can involve acceptor stem, discriminator base and other structural features|Each individual tRNA gene requires its own synthetase
A common CCA terminus is not sufficient to distinguish families. Different enzymes use different combinations of identity features.
MCQ
Which process directly produces fMet-tRNA in typical bacteria after initial charging?
CCA addition|Ribosomal translocation|RNA splicing|Formylation of Met-tRNA by a transformylase
MetRS charges the initiator RNA with methionine; a separate enzyme formylates it. Initiation machinery subsequently recognizes the product.
MCQ
Which method provides evidence of reversible amino acid activation?
ATP–PPi exchange|DNA restriction digest|Southern blot of a chromosome|Measurement of peptide length alone
Exchange can report reversible adenylate formation. It does not establish successful aminoacyl transfer; the other methods do not directly examine activation.
MCQ
A tRNA with an intact anticodon but no A76 will most directly fail at which task?
Codon complementarity in isolation|Ordinary aminoacyl ester formation|Transcription of mRNA|Hydrolysis of GTP by EF-G
The terminal ribose is the usual acceptor for the amino acid. Codon pairing information may remain even when cargo attachment fails.
Assertion–Reason

Assertion: A correctly paired tRNA can introduce an incorrect amino acid. Reason: The normal decoding center evaluates codon–anticodon pairing rather than independently verifying the attached side chain.
Both true, reason explains assertion|Both true, reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
The separation between RNA identity and cargo explains why mischarging can escape nucleotide-based decoding. This is not the claim that all mischarged tRNAs are delivered equally well.
Assertion–Reason
Assertion: Pre-transfer editing may occur in a complex containing tRNA. Reason: Pre-transfer editing is defined by the absence of amino acid transfer to RNA, not by the absence of RNA binding.
Both true, reason explains assertion|Both true, reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
A bound tRNA can stimulate editing of the adenylate before covalent transfer. The name describes reaction order.
Assertion–Reason
Assertion: The number of synthetase genes is exactly twenty in every cell. Reason: Some organisms generate Gln-tRNA^Gln by modifying Glu-tRNA^Gln.
Both true, reason explains assertion|Both true, reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
The indirect pathway is a counterexample to a universal twenty-gene rule. Other variation comes from compartment-specific enzymes and gene duplication.
Assertion–Reason
Assertion: A high charged fraction proves that translation is accurate. Reason: Some assays do not distinguish cognate from mischarged tRNA.
Both true, reason explains assertion|Both true, reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
A high esterified fraction can include wrong cargo. Measuring amino acid identity is a separate requirement.
Multiple statements
Which statements are correct? I. CCA can be added during maturation. II. A76 is the usual attachment platform. III. All tRNA genes encode CCA. IV. Synthetases add the CCA sequence.
I and II only|II and III only|III and IV only|All four
I and II are correct. CCA can be gene-encoded or added; its addition is a nucleotidyltransferase reaction, not aminoacylation.
Multiple statements
Which are correct? I. Class I and II share the overall reaction. II. Their folds differ. III. PheRS is class II. IV. Every class II enzyme uses 3′-OH initially.
I and IV|I, II and III|II and IV|All four
I–III are true; PheRS supplies an exception to IV.
Matching
Match 1. AlaRS 2. IleRS 3. SerRS 4. RelA-associated response with a. G3·U70 b. Val editing c. long variable arm d. uncharged tRNA signal.
The alanine determinant is in the acceptor stem; IleRS edits valine; canonical serine tRNAs use variable-arm recognition; uncharged tRNA participates in the bacterial stringent response.
